summary: The Parents Over Platforms Act sets rules for mobile application distributors and app developers regarding age assurance and the protection of minors. It creates responsibilities for verifying user ages, sharing age signals between distributors and developers, providing parental controls, banning personalized advertising for minors, and enforcing these rules through the Federal Trade Commission while preempting state laws.

affected_groups.effect: Under-18 users will have their age category shared via age signals (with parental agreement), be blocked from adult-only applications or restricted content, and cannot receive personalized advertising.
Parents are provided with mechanisms to prevent minors from acquiring specific apps, block age-rated content categories, and access privacy and safety settings information.
Entities operating app distributors must ask for age declarations, support parental control features, share age signals, and avoid using third-party data anticompetitively.

Developers of covered applications must report age distinctions, determine user ages with reasonable effort, obtain consent for minor access where required, restrict personalized ads, and limit the use of age data.

key_provisions: Application distribution providers must ask account holders to declare their age, provide a mechanism for updating age categories, and offer technical abilities to share age signals with developers.
Application distribution providers must give parents the ability to prevent minors from acquiring or using covered applications, and provide ways to block content categories by age rating.

Developers of covered applications must report whether their apps treat adults and minors differently, use commercially reasonable efforts to verify user ages, and block minors from adult-only content or activities.
Developers are strictly prohibited from delivering personalized advertising to minors.
Violations of this Act are treated as unfair or deceptive acts or practices enforced by the Federal Trade Commission.
State and local laws related to the provisions of this Act are fully preempted.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Parents Over Platforms Act sets rules for mobile application distributors and app developers regarding age assurance and the protection of minors. It creates responsibilities for verifying user ages, sharing age signals between distributors and developers, providing parental controls, banning personalized advertising for minors, and enforcing these rules through the Federal Trade Commission while preempting state laws.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a unified federal framework for age assurance and parental controls in the mobile app ecosystem, directly impacting how application distributors and developers handle minor accounts, age verification, and targeted advertising while removing state-level regulatory authority.
